sections.content:
Level 2 completed! Now on level 3. The new level has a different maze structure. Let me analyze the segmentation to understand the new layout. I can see:
- Player (blue) at bottom right
- Goal (green) at bottom left
- Multiple red cells scattered around
- White and gray cells forming a maze
Let me use segmentation to map out the maze structure.

sections.content: Level 2 completed! Now on level 3. Let me analyze the new maze structure.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']

# Find player, goal, and red cells
player_pos = None
goal_pos = None
red_cells = []
all_cells = {}

for n in nodes:
    if n['pixels'] <= 1:
        continue
    b = n['boundary']
    center_r = sum(p[0] for p in b) / len(b)
    center_c = sum(p[1] for p in b) / len(b)
    # Convert to maze coords (cell = center / 3, rounded)
    cr = round((center_r - 21) / 3)
    cc = round((center_c - 12) / 3)
    all_cells[(cr, cc)] = n['color']
    
    if n['color'] in ('b', 'c'):
        player_pos = (cr, cc)
        print(f"Player at maze ({cr},{cc}), center=({center_r:.0f},{center_c:.0f})")
    if n['color'] == 'N':
        goal_pos = (cr, cc)
        print(f"Goal at maze ({cr},{cc}), center=({center_r:.0f},{center_c:.0f})")
    if n['color'] == 'R':
        red_cells.append((cr, cc))
        print(f"Red at maze ({cr},{cc})")

print(f"\nAll cells: {sorted(all_cells.items())}")
print(f"\nPlayer: {player_pos}, Goal: {goal_pos}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
